guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is 0, service_rejected_error is cleared to 0.
When rst_ni is 1 and service_rejected_error_set is 1, service_rejected_error is set to 1, taking priority over any simultaneous service_rejected_error_clr assertion.
When rst_ni is 1 and service_rejected_error_set is 0 and service_rejected_error_clr is 1, service_rejected_error is cleared to 0.
If no set, clear, or reset condition is active, service_rejected_error retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni must be asserted (low) at least once before normal operation to initialize service_rejected_error to 0.
assumptions.risk: Without reset, the register starts with unknown (x) value, causing spurious error indications or missed errors in downstream logic.

assumptions.claim: External logic must not assert service_rejected_error_set when intending to clear the error via service_rejected_error_clr, because set takes priority and will prevent clearing.
assumptions.risk: The error flag remains stuck high, potentially hiding subsequent errors or causing a permanent fault state.

uncertain_points.claim: The priority of service_rejected_error_set over service_rejected_error_clr may be intentional (sticky error until set condition removed) or a design oversight. Intent is unclear from this chunk alone.
uncertain_points.cond: When both set and clr are asserted simultaneously or set remains high while clr is attempted
uncertain_points.risk: If unintended, error may never be cleared under some conditions, leading to a stuck fault indication and loss of error recovery.

uncertain_points.claim: If rst_ni is never asserted after power-up, service_rejected_error holds an unknown (x) value that may propagate to other logic and cause false or missed error responses.
uncertain_points.risk: System may enter an undefined fault state, potentially violating safety or security properties.
